summary:
ASTROQUEST is an interactive space survival game that introduces players to the challenges of managing an astronaut mission. Players make mission decisions, manage essential resources, respond to emergencies, and try to bring their crew safely through their space expedition.
Space exploration requires careful planning, teamwork, resource management, and quick decision-making.

ASTROQUEST turns these ideas into an interactive browser game where players experience the responsibilities of a junior astronaut and learn how decisions can affect a mission.
 Features
 Mission Destinations: Choose between Moon and Mars missions.
 Interactive Gameplay: Make decisions that influence mission outcomes.
 Resource Management: Monitor oxygen, water, food, energy, and crew health.
 Emergency Scenarios: Respond to unexpected mission challenges.
 Difficulty Levels: Choose Easy, Normal, or Hard.
 Achievements: Unlock badges by completing gameplay milestones.
 Flight Records: Track personal scores and mission achievements.
 Sound Effects: Toggle game audio on or off.
 Mission Reports: Review your performance at the end of a mission.
 Local Progress: Save supported game records in your browser.
 Responsive Interface: Play on supported desktop and mobile browsers.
details:
ASTROQUEST – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

ASTROQUEST is an educational space-mission simulator. It lets players live the role of a mission commander during a journey to the Moon or Mars. Players must make choices manage supplies like oxygen, water and food and keep the crew safe from unexpected dangers. It’s a way to learn about space missions and the tough decisions involved.

Working:

Players start by picking a difficulty level—Easy, Normal or Hard—and choosing a destination: Mission Luna (Moon) or Mission Ares (Mars). Once the mission begins they watch five indicators: oxygen, water, food, energy and crew health. These are the keys to survival. As the mission unfolds sudden emergencies will appear—like a power failure or an oxygen leak. Players must pick the response from a few options. Each choice changes the mission outcome. It might save resources. Cost them affect crew safety or delay progress. At the end a full mission report shows what happened and the Flight Record keeps track of achievements, missions and top scores.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

ASTROQUEST makes learning about space easy. It works great for students and young learners who're curious about science. It helps build thinking skills like problem-solving, planning and making decisions fast under pressure. It also shows how important things like oxygen, water and healthy crew are during space travel. Our goal is to spark interest in space and make studying STEM subjects fun and hands-on.

Technology Used:

We built ASTROQUEST using HTML, CSS and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code. HTML sets up the structure of the game. CSS takes care of the look—colors, animations and how it works on phones and computers. JavaScript runs the game engine handles mission events tracks resources, scores points and lets players interact. Browser Local Storage saves data like high scores, achievements and sound settings. The Web Audio API gives us effects to make the experience feel real. The game runs in a web browser. No downloads no setup—just open it and play.


Creativity and innovation:

ASTROQUEST stands out by mixing space adventure with strategy and survival. Of just reading about astronaut life players jump into realistic but simplified mission situations. They learn by making choices and seeing the results. The game offers planets, difficulty levels, emergencies and rewards. Achievements and personal high scores give players a reason to play again and again. It's not a game—it's a learning experience wrapped in action.

Factors Considered:

We thought about things while building the game. We wanted it to be easy to use clear to understand and fun to play. We made sure it works well on all screens from phones to desktops. We balanced resources so players feel challenged but not overwhelmed. We made sure every decision matters so players learn from mistakes. We added difficulty levels so kids of all ages can enjoy it. We kept the scenarios educational—this is not a real mission simulator but a tool to teach and inspire.

We used ChatGPT to help with some parts of the project. It helped us with fixing bugs in our code and improving the user interface and writing project documentation. AI was a helper, not a creator.
